finding.claim: SQL injection via unvalidated ORDER BY column taken from the sort GET parameter in list_users_sorted. ORDER BY cannot be parameterized and no allowlist is applied, so an attacker can inject arbitrary SQL expressions (e.g. boolean/blind subqueries, CASE WHEN (SELECT ...)) to exfiltrate data from any table in the SQLite DB. Stacked queries are unlikely with query(), but blind extraction works. Note list_users_safe uses an allowlist and is fine.
finding.sink: $pdo->query("SELECT id, name FROM users ORDER BY " . $sort) at list.php:6

trace.note: Concatenated directly into the SQL string and executed via PDO::query

finding.guards_checked: No allowlist, no escaping, no auth check in the file. Searched the directory: list.php is the only file, so no upstream middleware. Prepared statements are not used for this query. Caveat: list_users_sorted is not called anywhere in this file, so reachability depends on an external caller; reported because the function reads $_GET directly and the file is a standalone PHP entry point.

verdict.reason: list.php:5-6 reads $_GET['sort'] and concatenates it unvalidated into the ORDER BY of a PDO::query, with no allowlist (unlike list_users_safe at list.php:10-11); the only caveat is that nothing in this directory calls list_users_sorted, so exposure depends on an external caller.
